column1: # The authored acquisition-rung expectation for the Phase-26 bake catalog.
# `image_build_doctrine.md` §7 orders the ladder: an `apt` package where an official one
# exists, otherwise an official multi-arch artifact verified against the publisher's own
# checksum manifest resolved at build time, otherwise build-from-source. Extracting a binary
# out of a public image sits *below* rung 3, and every retained use records why the rungs
# §M.3: this table is the reference side, authored independently of `BakeCatalog.dhall` and
# never imported from it. It is authored *before* the catalog gains its arms, so the
# chronology is Git-established. A catalog reconciled against its own value would pass for any
# catalog, including one that scavenges everything.
# Every row was verified against the publisher or the archive, for BOTH linux/amd64 and
# linux/arm64, before it was written here — not recalled. The apt rows were confirmed against
# `apt-cache policy` in a real `ubuntu:24.04` container and against the `ports.ubuntu.com`
# arm64 `Packages` index; the official-artifact rows were confirmed by fetching the asset and
# the publisher's own checksum manifest and running the checksum comparison.
# The result worth stating plainly: **no binary needs the scavenge rung.** The catalog this
# table describes has zero `CopyOci` steps, against 22 in the pre-amendment catalog, so the
# 35 hand-maintained `supportCopies` entries that carried other images' shared-library
# name<TAB>rung<TAB>what was verified, and for a CopyOci row why the rungs above did not apply
# --- rung 1: apt, where Ubuntu 24.04 ships the binary for both arches ------------------

releases.hashicorp.com zip for both arches with the release's own SHA256SUMS. Verified 2026-08-14: vault_1.20.2_linux_{amd64,arm64}.zip both 200; one release-level manifest naming both, sha256, digest+name, zip archive holding the bare `vault`

github prometheus/prometheus v3.5.0 tarballs for both arches; sha256sums.txt in the same release covers both and was checked with sha256sum -c. Verified 2026-08-14 through the release API: prometheus-3.5.0.linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz and sha256sums.txt all present; sha256, digest+name, tar.gz whose top directory carries the arch

github prometheus/alertmanager v0.28.1 tarballs for both arches with the release's sha256sums.txt. Verified 2026-08-14 through the release API: alertmanager-0.28.1.linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz and sha256sums.txt all present; sha256, digest+name, tar.gz

github thanos-io/thanos v0.39.2 tarballs for both arches with the release's checksum manifest. Verified 2026-08-14 through the release API: thanos-0.39.2.linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz and sha256sums.txt all present; sha256, digest+name, tar.gz

the published Envoy release binaries for both arches; from-source is Bazel, which amoebius does not adopt. Verified 2026-08-14: envoy-1.35.1-linux-x86_64 and envoy-1.35.1-linux-aarch_64 (publisher's own spelling), bare binaries. ANOMALY: the only manifest is checksums.txt.asc, a PGP-clearsigned sha256 list whose entries name the publisher's build paths (/tmp/tmp<random>/bin/<asset>), so verification must match the trailing basename and cannot feed the line to `sha256sum -c`. The armor is not itself checked, so this is a digest claim, not a signature check

the Grafana download tarballs for both arches with the publisher's own checksum. Verified 2026-08-14: grafana-12.1.1.linux-{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz both 200; per-asset .sha256 manifest whose body is the bare digest with no filename, so there is nothing to match on; tar.gz holding the whole install tree

github keycloak/keycloak 26.3.2 distribution tarball, arch-independent JVM payload, with the release's checksum. Verified 2026-08-14 through the release API: keycloak-26.3.2.tar.gz present and named by both arch rows. ANOMALY: the publisher offers .md5, .sha1, and .asc and no sha256 — the strongest digest manifest Keycloak publishes is SHA-1, whose collision resistance is broken. The stronger option is the .asc PGP signature, which needs an authored trust anchor this phase does not yet have; the SHA-1 claim is recorded as what the publisher offers, not as adequate

the Apache dist archives for Pulsar 4.0.6 and its separately published offloader bundle, each verified with Apache's own .sha512; both are architecture-independent JVM payloads. The main release manifest remains on downloads.apache.org while its rolled-off tarball is read from archive.apache.org; the offloader archive and manifest are both read from the archive. sha512, digest+./name, tar.gz holding the install tree and /pulsar/offloaders NARs
